questions.question_text: What is the $5\text{th}$ term in the expansion of $(x - 2)^{7}$?

options.why: Applied a negative sign to $(-2)^4$, forgetting that an even power of a negative is positive.
Used $r=5$ for the 5th term instead of $r=4$, giving $\binom{7}{5}x^{2}(-2)^{5}$.
Used $r=3$ instead of $r=4$, finding the 4th term rather than the 5th term.

questions.question_text: Find the coefficient of $x^{3}$ in the expansion of $(2x - 3)^{5}$.

options.why: Squared $-3$ as $-9$ instead of $+9$ when evaluating the numerical factor.
Used $r=3$ (the power of $x$) instead of $r=2$, evaluating $\binom{5}{3}2^{2}(-3)^{3}$.
Omitted the constant factor $(-3)^{2}$ from the product evaluation.

questions.question_text: Find the term independent of $x$ in the expansion of $\left(3x^{2} + \dfrac{1}{x}\right)^{6}$.

options.why: Used $r=2$ instead of $r=4$, evaluating $\binom{6}{2}3^{4} = 15 \times 81$.
Omitted the base coefficient $3^{2}$, calculating only the combination $\binom{6}{4}$.
Multiplied $6 \times 3^{4} = 486$ incorrectly by confusing term indices.

questions.question_text: Find the term containing $x^{2}y^{3}$ in the expansion of $(3x - 2y)^{5}$.

options.why: Omitted the negative sign resulting from the odd power $(-2)^{3}=-8$.
Swapped the powers of $x$ and $y$, evaluating the term in $x^{3}y^{2}$.
Used $3^{1}$ instead of $3^{2}$ when raising the first term to power $5-3$.

questions.question_text: Find the $4\text{th}$ term in the expansion of $(2x^{2} + 1)^{8}$.

options.why: Used $r = 4$ for the 4th term instead of $r = 3$, so this is really the 5th term: $\binom{8}{4}2^{4}x^{8} = 70 \times 16x^{8}$.
Left the $2$ in $(2x^{2})^{5}$ as a single factor instead of raising it to the power $5$, giving $56 \times 2 = 112$ rather than $56 \times 32$.
Made both slips at once: took $r = 4$ instead of $r = 3$, and kept the $2$ unraised, giving $70 \times 2 = 140$.

questions.question_text: Which of the following binomial expansions has a non-zero constant term when expanded?

options.why: Setting the index equation $16-5r=0$ gives $r=3.2$, which is not an integer.
Setting the index equation $28-5r=0$ gives $r=5.6$, which is not an integer.
Setting the index equation $14-3r=0$ gives $r=4.\dot{6}$, which is not an integer.

questions.solution_text:
$T_{r+1} = \binom{10}{r}(x^{3})^{10-r}\left(-\dfrac{2}{x^{2}}\right)^{r}$
$= \binom{10}{r}(-2)^{r}x^{30-5r}$
$\text{For } x^{0}\text{, let } 30 - 5r = 0\text{, giving } r = 6\text{ (an integer).}$
$\text{Constant term} = \binom{10}{6}(-2)^{6} = 13440 \neq 0$

questions.question_text: Find the coefficient of $x^{2}$ in the expansion of $\left(x^{3} - \dfrac{2}{x}\right)^{6}$.

options.why: Treated $(-2)^4$ as negative instead of positive $16$.
Used $r=2$ instead of $r=4$, calculating $\binom{6}{2}(-2)^{2} = 15 \times 4$.
Omitted the base multiplier $(-2)^{4}$, recording only the combination $\binom{6}{4}$.

questions.question_text: Find the coefficient of $x^{4}y^{6}$ in the expansion of $(x^{2} - 3y^{3})^{4}$.

options.why: Squared $-3$ as $-9$ instead of $+9$ when evaluating the numerical power.
Omitted the combination coefficient $\binom{4}{2}=6$, multiplying $2 \times 9$.
Used $r=3$ instead of $r=2$, evaluating $\binom{4}{3}(-3)^{3} = -108$.

questions.question_text: In the expansion of $(1 + kx)^{8}$, where $k$ is a positive constant, the coefficient of $x^{2}$ is $252$. What is the value of $k$?

options.why: Found $k^{2}=9$ but forgot to take the square root to find $k$.
Included the negative solution $-3$ despite the stem specifying $k > 0$.
Divided $252$ by $\binom{8}{1}=8$ or made an arithmetic error solving $k^{2}=36$.
